claim_text: Samsung Securities says an outside party got into its customer-feedback system
summary: Samsung Securities said an unauthorized outside party accessed the Voice of the Customer (VOC) system on its website and took some files customers had uploaded. Press reports relay its statement.
detail: Detected Sat Nov 21 (Korea time) per the company. Korea Times/Yonhap calls it a "customer response website". The company's own notice was not retrievable, so this rests on press accounts of its statement.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Yonhap, The Herald Business and Hankyoreh each attribute the finding to Samsung Securities.
notes: Company statement relayed by press; outlets relaying it count as one source.

claim_text: Samsung Securities says data of 8,241 clients was leaked
summary: Samsung Securities told press that data of 8,241 clients was leaked after the intrusion. The Korea Times/Yonhap text says "more than 8,000".
detail: The count is the company's own finding. No outside check or regulator figure found.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Yonhap and the Herald Business give 8,241 as the company's count.
notes: Company statement relayed by press; outlets relaying it count as one source.

claim_text: The data included names, account numbers, addresses and driver's license numbers
summary: Samsung Securities says 13 kinds of personal data were involved, including name, account number, address, contact details and driver's license number. What each client lost varies.
detail: The data came from attachments clients uploaded with VOC submissions, per Yonhap. The Korea Times text names only names and addresses.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Press attribute the list of data types to the company.
notes: Company statement relayed by press; outlets relaying it count as one source.

claim_text: Samsung Securities says only clients who used the VOC form were affected
summary: Samsung Securities says leak traces were found only in VOC submissions, and that clients who did not file one are not involved. It says other customer information was not affected.
detail: This is the company's own scoping, with no outside check. The company says it is still checking other systems.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Press attribute the scope to the company.
notes: Company statement relayed by press; outlets relaying it count as one source.

claim_text: Samsung Securities says it blocked the intruder and reported the breach
summary: Samsung Securities says it blocked the IP address, suspended the VOC service, reported to the financial regulator and the internet security agency, and will notify affected clients one by one.
detail: It also says it will pay compensation if actual harm is confirmed. No regulator statement found.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Press attribute these steps to the company.
notes: Company statement relayed by press; outlets relaying it count as one source.

summary: Samsung Securities describes access by "abnormal means" and says it is still investigating the cause. No source says how the intruder got in.
detail: Whether the files were copied in bulk or how many times the system was reached is not stated.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company has not given a method; the press reports repeat that it is investigating.

summary: No source we read names the attacker, and we found no claim of responsibility in the press we read.
detail: We did not look at leak sites, forums or trackers.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company calls the intruder "an unauthorized outside party" and press name no one.

claim_text: The breach is linked to the Samsung Ads vendor breach or a Samsung Group leak claim
summary: No source we read links the Samsung Securities breach to the Samsung Ads vendor breach or to any leak claim naming Samsung Group.
detail: Different business, different system and different data. A shared brand name is not evidence of a link. We did not look at leak sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No article about this breach mentions either.

claim_text: It is the latest in a run of breaches at Korean financial firms
summary: Yonhap and The Herald Business say it follows breaches at other Korean securities firms, naming Daishin, Hanyang and Mirae Asset, and a wider wave at financial firms.
detail: Context only. Neither article says the incidents are connected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both articles describe the earlier breaches.
